## Setting

<!-- ~10 lines. Build the object in this order, one sentence each:
     - a quantum network is a graph whose edges are two copies of a
       pure partially entangled state |psi> = sqrt(l0)|00> +
       sqrt(l1)|11>, l0 >= l1;
     - the singlet conversion probability (SCP) of a single copy is
       p = min[1, 2(1 - l0)];
     - two copies without distillation give p_2 = 2p - p^2; with
       distillation the largest Schmidt coefficient of |psi>^{x2} gives
       p_2 = min(1, 2p - p^2/2). Define "with/without distillation"
       here once and use the terms consistently afterwards;
     - classical entanglement percolation (CEP) = apply the conversion
       independently to every edge, so the network becomes bond
       percolation with occupation probability p_2;
     - once a path of singlets exists, entanglement swapping connects
       the endpoints, so two arbitrary nodes are connected with
       probability S^2 where S is the GCC relative size.
     Cite [@acin2007entanglement] for CEP and [@cuquet2009entanglement]
     throughout. -->

$$
p \;=\; \min\!\left[1,\, 2(1-\lambda_0)\right],
\qquad
p_2 \;=\;
\begin{cases}
2p - p^2, & \text{without distillation},\\[2pt]
\min\!\left(1,\, 2p - p^2/2\right), & \text{with distillation}.
\end{cases}
$$ {#eq-scp}

## The $q$-swap

<!-- ~8 lines + the schematic. Explain:
     - entanglement swapping at a central node c: a Bell measurement on
       two qubits belonging to states shared with a and b creates an
       edge a-b with the same SCP p as the original edges;
     - the q-swap performs swaps between successive pairs of neighbours
       of a degree-q node, turning a q-star into a q-cycle and
       detaching the central node;
     - the operation is LOCAL: it needs only the target's degree and
       the status of its neighbours;
     - constraint: no two q-swaps on neighbouring sites;
     - the strategy is specified by the set {gamma_q}, the probability
       of applying a q-swap on degree-q nodes. Note the paper's result
       that the optimum has every gamma_q in {0, 1}.
